answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by binding each identity to a locked bond that its shared kernel enforces. To count, an agent posts stake and emits a signed pulse that peers verify, while an independent raven monitor cross-checks timing to flag personas reusing keys or behavior. Any duplicate found this way forfeits its bond, so an attacker must lock fresh capital for every fake identity and can lose all of it once detected, making the cost climb with each clone.
